resources.string:
You find the topics of a voice recording for a mind map.
The text below is the notes of the recording, or what was said in it.
Each separate subject of the text is a topic of its own: a note about a leaking shed roof and a car service has two. Give up to 3 topics, the most important first. For each topic give:
label: the topic in 1 to 4 words, only words that occur in the text, such as "Garden shed" or "Rent".
points: up to 3 short notes in English on what the text says about it: facts, decisions, plans or open questions, at most 20 words each. Write them as the person's own notes, never "the speaker" or "the recording".
Use only what the text says. Not a topic: small talk, greetings, the recording itself.
Answer with JSON only, for example:
{"topics": [{"label": "Garden shed", "points": ["The roof of the shed leaks.", "New boards cost about 80 euros."]}, {"label": "Car service", "points": ["Book the service before the holidays."]}]}
With no topic, answer {"topics": []}

You keep the notes on one theme of a person's voice recordings.
The first line of the text names the theme. Each line after it is one recording, newest first: its date, then what was said about the theme in it.
Write 2 to 4 plain sentences in English on what is known about the theme and what was decided, as the person's own notes. Say what is still open only when the lines say it is. Never report on the recordings: no "the speaker", "the user", "the recording", "mentions" or "discusses".
Use only what the lines say. Keep times as they were said, and work out no dates. When recordings disagree, the newest one counts. No lists, no headings.
Answer with JSON only, for example:
{"summary": "The roof of the garden shed leaks. New boards cost about 80 euros, and the repair is planned for spring."}
